chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of his companions, from Musanna al-Hannat and al-Hasan al-Sayqal, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fasting person who immerses himself in water. He said: 'No,' and (also) the one in Ihram. He said, 'And I asked him about the fasting person who wears the wet garment. He said: 'No'.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The one in Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj/Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Does a fasting person's fast break if they immerse themselves in water or wear wet clothes?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies that full immersion (gartamus) or wearing wet garments does not invalidate the fast, addressing a specific juristic concern about whether such acts constitute eating, drinking, or sexual intercourse. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between ritual purification acts and the primary nullifiers of fasting, ensuring that necessary hygiene practices do not inadvertently break the fast.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from one of his companions, from Musna Al Hannat and Al Hassan Al Sayqal who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Fasting one immersing himself into the water. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, and neither can the one in Ihraam’. 
He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the Fasting one wearing the dripping wet clothes. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from certain persons of our people from Muthanna’ al-Hannat and al- Hassan al-Sayqal who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is fasting and immerses himself in water. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he must not do so and also one who is in the state of Ihram.’
He (the narrator) has said that he asked him (the Imam) about one who is fasting, puts on wet clothes. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he must not do so.’”
